results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 56 aligned units match the controlling idea of their spec paragraph (p01-p57, no p13 in the spec) in spec order; the five opening callouts are unaligned, as the spec declares no paragraphs for them.

One unit marked two_ideas (In Practice ¶6, Motorvane ghost and Hearthly duplicates). Its lead sentence ('Two of the book's other worked examples ... show the counter-metrics at work') states one idea with two instances, exactly as spec p37 declares.

Every unit ties to a supporting claim: scene and concepts to L1/L2, competing to L3, tree and failure modes to L4, practice to L2/L4, requirements, Chief Architect's view and questions to L5, trade-offs to L4, vertical differences to L3.

results.quote: a16z's 2020 list of marketplace metrics includes the "prevalence of multi-tenanting" as a defensibility measure
results.finding: The a16z citation is the last sentence of the paragraph, placed after the architecture consequence; no sentence says what it shows or how it bears on the point that differentiation must come from what the platform does with non-exclusive inventory. Both flow readers read it as a leftover citation (flow-a item 9, flow-b item 9).

results.quote: Answering it starts with two-sided markets.
results.finding: The declared known information (the meeting's new question about which Portuguese cells can become liquid) is picked up only by the pronoun 'it' directly after a section heading, so the elaboration has no visible antecedent; both flow readers had to look back to resolve it (flow-a item 1, flow-b item 1).

results.quote: NFX describes multi-tenanting as occurring when there are "low costs or no costs to simultaneously participating in competing networks"
results.finding: The boundary is declared cause_effect, carrying over multi-homing's forms, with the transition at the start of the paragraph. The opening sentence instead introduces a quotation under a new term (multi-tenanting) that is never tied to multi-homing; the cause-effect move ('The architecture consequence is direct.') arrives only in the second sentence.

results.quote: **Vanity metrics on the wall.** The most common failure is a dashboard of inputs
results.finding: Declared contrast carrying over how the metrics should differ by vertical; the section opens directly on its first failure with no phrase that picks up the vertical differences or marks the turn from how metrics should work to how they go wrong. Flow-a marked the section's position unclear.

results.quote: Answering it starts with two-sided markets.
results.finding: After the heading, 'it' has no nearby referent; flow-a had to look back to find it meant the Portuguese-cells question, and flow-b adds that the promised link to Portugal never appears in the section.

results.quote: Scout24's results show that consumers will pay for an advantage in such a market.
results.finding: A revenue statistic inside the definition of same-side effects pulls the reader away from the concept (flow-a item 2).

results.quote: This book also draws on a reference model I maintain: a generic description of how a general-listings marketplace works, modeled on no real company
results.finding: A new source and a sudden first-person voice introduced inside the third bullet of the liquidity definition interrupt it; flow-a had to re-read to see the quotations come from this model (flow-a item 3).

results.quote: The mechanism behind these numbers is a combination of local cross-side effects and an asymmetry in **multi-homing** (using several competing platforms at once).
results.finding: Multi-homing and its asymmetry are used as the mechanism before they are explained, then defined again in their own subsection; both readers propose moving Multi-homing before Winner-take-most. The spec places the gloss here and the definition after the limits paragraph, so the difficulty comes from the declared order.

results.quote: Bill Gurley's 2012 list of marketplace factors explains why these markets tip
results.finding: Flow-a could not see how fragmentation explains tipping and read the paragraph as an aside; flow-b read it as a second explanation of why markets tip right after 'the mechanism', unsure which one the chapter means.

results.quote: Its "stock" lever, the number of paid vehicles retailers advertise, subtracted £48 from average revenue per retailer
results.finding: Investor jargon in a dense sentence; flow-a re-read it (flow-a item 7).

results.quote: a16z's 2020 list of marketplace metrics includes the "prevalence of multi-tenanting" as a defensibility measure
